text:
Matt Coronato's season so far reads as a setup man's year: 15 points in 21 games, 11 of them assists, seven on the power play. The goals have been slower. He has four on 4.57 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 9.1%, a little under his talent range, so there is no luck to blame, just fewer looks than last season. His own chances have dropped to 0.74 expected goals per 60 from 0.99.

The biggest moment was a good one: the overtime winner against the Flyers on Nov. 8, part of a rally. Outside that night and a four-point game against Seattle on Oct. 30, though, he has been held off the scoresheet in eight of his last ten games.

The worry is the other end. Calgary gets only 44.15% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on, worse than when he sits, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating far more with him on the ice last season (bottom 1% of forwards). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking showed what he does well: 8.5 home-plate chances per 60, 98th percentile. Watch whether those chances come back.
headline: Matt Coronato is creating more than he's finishing
